articles.title: Tesla gets support from S . Korean retail investors amid downward slide

articles.article_title: Tesla gets support from S.Korean retail investors amid downward slide
articles.article_text: Retail investors in South Korea have bought $2.8 billion worth of Tesla ( NASDAQ:TSLA ) stock despite its downward slide these last few months. According to the Korea Securities Depository, day traders bought $160 million worth of Tesla shares up through December 27, 2022. South Korean retail investors continue to buy TSLA stocks amid its downward slide. As of this writing, Tesla’s stock price stands at $109.10 per share, down 11.41%. The company’s market cap took a hit, now standing at $344.51 billion. Tesla stock is down 69% in 2022 and has dropped 73% compared to its record high in November 2021. Bloomberg notes that despite its downward slide, Tesla remains a popular overseas stock among South Korean retail investors. In August 2022, Teslarati reported that Tesla fans in S. Korea amassed $15 billion worth of TSLA stock , amounting to 1.6% of the company. Like most TSLA bulls, South Korean retail investors are taking advantage of the current Tesla share price and buying at the dip. Tesla remains a popular brand in Asia, and Elon Musk is still a popular figure in the region. Tesla is strengthening its presence in Asia. Recently, the office of President Yoon Suk-Yeol shared that Elon Musk considered building a factory in South Korea. President Yoon later stated that he would be open to offering Tesla tailored incentives if it builds a gigafactory in the country. Telsa is expected to announce the location of its new gigafactory before the year ends. The company was rumored to announce it last week, but Tesla kept mum about a new gigafactory. Mexico, Indonesia, and Canada are the other countries vying to be the location of Tesla’s new gigafactory . Do you know anything about Tesla’s next gigafactory location? This strategy should allow Tesla to scale more profitably compared to Robotaxi competitors, helped by a growing data engine from its existing fleet,” BoA wrote. Tesla received a tip of the hat from major Wall Street firm Bank of America on Wednesday, as it reinitiated coverage on Tesla shares with a bullish stance that comes with a ‘Buy’ rating and a $460 price target. In a new note that marks a sharp reversal from its neutral position earlier in 2025 , the bank declared Tesla’s Full Self-Driving (FSD) technology the “leading consumer autonomy solution.” Analysts highlighted Tesla’s camera-only architecture, known as Tesla Vision , as a strategic masterstroke. While technically more challenging than the multi-sensor setups favored by rivals, the vision-based approach is dramatically cheaper to produce and maintain. This cost edge, combined with Tesla’s rapidly expanding real-world data engine, positions the company to scale robotaxis far more profitably than competitors, BofA argues in the new note: “Tesla is at the forefront of autonomous driving, supported by a camera-only approach that is technically harder but much cheaper than the multi-sensor systems widely used in the industry. This strategy should allow Tesla to scale more profitably compared to Robotaxi competitors, helped by a growing data engine from its existing fleet.” The bank now attributes roughly 52% of Tesla’s total valuation to its Robotaxi ambitions. It also flagged meaningful upside from the Optimus humanoid robot program and the fast-growing energy storage business, suggesting the auto segment’s recent headwinds, including expired incentives, are being eclipsed by these higher-margin opportunities. Tesla’s own data underscores exactly why Wall Street is waking up to FSD’s potential. According to Tesla’s official safety reporting page, the FSD Supervised fleet has now surpassed 8.4 billion cumulative miles driven. Tesla FSD (Supervised) fleet passes 8.4 billion cumulative miles That total ballooned from just 6 million miles in 2021 to 80 million in 2022, 670 million in 2023, 2.25 billion in 2024, and a staggering 4.25 billion in 2025 alone. In the first 50 days of 2026, owners added another 1 billion miles — averaging more than 20 million miles per day. This avalanche of real-world, camera-captured footage, much of it on complex city streets, gives Tesla an unmatched training dataset. Every mile feeds its neural networks, accelerating improvement cycles that lidar-dependent rivals simply cannot match at scale.

articles.title: La movida inesperada de Cathie Wood que sacude al mercado : apostó a un CEDEAR que cayó 82 % anual
articles.title_clean: La movida inesperada de Cathie Wood que sacude al mercado : apostó a un CEDEAR que cayó 82 % anual
articles.article_title: La movida inesperada de Cathie Wood que sacude al mercado: apostó a un CEDEAR que cayó 82% anual - El Cronista
articles.article_text: El CEDEAR por el que apuesta Cathie Wood Tras sucesivas compras la CEO de ARK Invest, Cathie Wood , continúa apostando por la suba de uno de los principales CEDEARs arbitrados en las cuentas comitentes de Argentina , que tuvo una estrepitosa caída durante el 2022, pero que por su relevancia continuó siendo uno de los papeles más consignados en los informes de las compañías financieras. Los mercados bursátiles globales cotizaban con pocos cambios el miércoles, luego de que China diera nuevos pasos hacia la reapertura de su maltrecha economía, debido a que las esperanzas de un repunte económico eran atenuadas por las preocupaciones sobre un aumento de casos de COVID-19 a corto plazo. El índice mundial se encamina a cerrar 2022 con una caída del 19,5%, su peor resultado desde la crisis financiera de 2008 , presionado por una inflación en máximos de varias décadas en las economías occidentales, la subida de las tasas de interés por parte de los principales bancos centrales y las estrictas políticas de cero COVID de China. Esta coyuntura afectó al desempeño anual de las principales compañías de valor relevadas por el S&P 500 , que perdieron mayormente frente a los papeles de empresas de bienes y servicios elásticos a las crisis. Cathie Wood continúa comprando acciones de Tesla (TSLA), que mostró un retroceso de 82% en el último año , ya que su administradora de activos manejada por su equipo recogió más de 25.000 acciones del gigante de los vehículos eléctricos a pesar de su reciente racha de pérdidas de siete días. En total, Wood adquirió 25.147 acciones de TSLA a través de su ETF insignia ARK Innovation (ARKK) el martes, según los registros comerciales de ARK. La afluencia de acciones de TSLA se sumó al total actual de 133.194 acciones de TSLA que Ark Invest ha comprado durante la racha de pérdidas de siete días de TSLA, que comenzó el 16 de diciembre . 27/12: ARKK compró 25.147 acciones de Tesla 23/12: ARKK compró 20.458 acciones de Tesla 21/12: ARKK compró 9.952 acciones de Tesla 20/12: ARKK compró 19.125 acciones de Tesla 19/12: ARKQ compró 27.494 acciones de Tesla 16/12: ARKK compró 31.018 acciones de Tesla El pronóstico alcista de Wood y su equipo determinaron que el fondo ARKK tenga a TSLA en la lista como su quinta participación más grande con un 6% , con un valor de mercado de u$s 346,08 millones. ARKQ, por otro lado, también calificó a TSLA como el quinto fondo más importante con un 6,98%, lo que equivale a un valor de mercado de 53,62 millones de dólares. Mientras que ARKK y los otros ETF de Wood tuvieron problemas en 2022, el equipo de Equity de Citibank relevó los 10 CEDEARs que podrían tomarse revancha el año próximo tras las caídas de este año, entre los que se encuentra Tesla.
